Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : BM1002 : Introduction to Bioengineering { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1
Introduction: Definition and branches of bioengineering, challenges and opportunities for bioengineers.
Basic biological systems: macromolecules (DNA, RNA, proteins, lipids, carbohydrates), Cells, Tissue, Organ Systems, microbial system (bacteria, fungi, viruses, microalgae), microbiomes.
Module 2
Fundamentals of engineering: Transport processes: mass, momentum and energy balance, Laminar/Turbulent flows, Analysis of basic differential equations Thermodynamics: Laws of thermodynamics, equations of states, thermodynamic relationships Kinetics: enzyme kinetics computational sciences: Data collection, analysis tools and modelling.
Module 3
Applications of bioengineering: Biomaterials design for drug delivery, implants and tissue engineering biosensors for diagnostic devices engineering microbes for production of biopharmaceutical drugs, biochemicals, and biofuels, environmental remediation imaging and image processing for diagnostics/surgical applications Medical devices: extracorporeal devices, assistive technologies, Ethics in Bioengineering.
Module 4
AI in bioengineering: Overview of basic terminologies, formulation of problems, Regression and neural network analysis.

Course Objective

1 .

To aware students about the role of bioengineers
2 .

To understand the complexity and elegance of biological machines at different length scales.
3 .

To understand how basic engineering principles help in understanding biological functions.
4 .

To understand how systematic engineering knowledge and tools helps to engineer biological system.
5. To understand various avenues for application of bioengineering in healthcare and biotech industries

Course Outcome

1 .

1. Gain foundational understanding of bioengineering in terms of its opportunities and challenges
2. Understand the role of basic biological principles for bio-based design
3. Integrate the fundamentals of engineering with basic biological rudiments for design based thinking
4. Understand the avenues for diverse applications of bioengineering
5. Gain basic knowledge of artificial intelligence and its application in the field of bioengineering

Essential Reading

1 .

Bird, R. B., Stewart, W. E., & Lightfoot, E. N., Transport phenomena, Wiley , 2nd ed

2 .

Fogler, H. Scott., Elements of Chemical Reaction Engineering, Pearson , 6th ed

Supplementary Reading

1 .

Alberts, B., Johnson, A., Lewis, J., Raff, M., Roberts, K., & Walter, P., Molecular biology of the cell, Garland Science , 6th ed

2 .

Smith, J. M., Van Ness, H. C., & Abbott, M. M., Introduction to chemical engineering thermodynamics, McGraw-Hill Education , 8th ed

6439.t: CE6201: Matrix Method of Structural Analysis
6439.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : CE6201 : Matrix Method of Structural Analysis { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Introduction: Matrix algebra, basic concepts of structural analysis. [6 hours]
Module 2 :

Flexibility matrix method: Introduction to the flexibility approach, derivation of flexibility matrix for bar, truss, beam, and frame structures, analysis of bar, truss, beam, and frame structures using flexibility matrix method. [10 hours]
Module 3 :

Stiffness matrix method: Introduction to the stiffness approach, derivation of stiffness matrix for bar, truss, beam, and frame structures, analysis of bar, truss, beam, and frame structures using stiffness matrix method. [10 hours]
Module 4 :

Direct stiffness method: Introduction to the direct stiffness method, derivation of member stiffness matrix using direct stiffness method for prismatic members, analysis of bar, plane truss, beam, plane frame, space truss, grid, and space frame structures using direct stiffness method, development of MATLAB codes for the analysis of skeletal structures using direct stiffness method. [10 hours]

Course Objective

1 .

Students will be able to perform matrix computations.
2 .

Students will be able to develop flexibility and stiffness matrix for prismatic members.
3 .

Students will be able to develop member stiffness matrix using direct stiffness method for prismatic members.
4 .

Students will be able to analyze bar, truss, beam, and frame structures using matrix method.

Course Outcome

1 .

To analyze skeletal structures for redundant actions using the flexibility matrix method.
2 .

To analyze skeletal structures for unknown joint displacements, member end actions, and support reactions using the flexibility matrix method.
3 .

To analyze skeletal structures using the stiffness matrix method.
4 .

To determine stiffness matrices and analyze bar, plane truss, beam, and plane frame structures using the direct stiffness method.
5 .

To determine stiffness matrices and analyze space truss, grid, and space frame structures using the direct stiffness method.

Essential Reading

1 .

W. Weaver, J. M. Gere, Matrix Analysis Framed Structures, Springer US

2 .

G. S. Pandit and S. P. Gupta, Structural Analysis: A Matrix Approach, Tata McGraw-Hill

Supplementary Reading

1 .

P. Nagarajan, Matrix Methods of Structural Analysis, CRC Press

2 .

A. Kassimali, Matrix Analysis of Structures, CL Engineering

Journal and Conferences

1 .

7207.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : EC4508 : Mobile Communication { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module 1: Introduction to Wireless Communication Systems [4 hrs.]
Evolution, Mobile Systems around the World, Example of the mobile radio systems, Recent trends, 2G, 3G and 4G Cellular networks.
Module 2: The Cellular Concept [5 hrs.]
Frequency reuse, Channel assignment, Hand off process, Types of Interference, Cellular capacity
Module 3: Mobile Radio Propagation [5 hrs.]
Path loss, Radio wave propagation, Reflection, Diffraction, Scattering, Link budget Design, Outdoor and indoor propagation models
Module 4: Principle of multi-path propagation [5 hrs.]
Impulse response model of channels, parameters for mobile multi-path channels, the concept of fading, Rayleigh and Ricean fading, Simulation of fading channels.
Pulse shaping, Linear and non-linear Modulation techniques, constant envelop modulation, QPSK, MSK, GMSK. Spread spectrum modulation techniques - Direct sequence and Frequency Hopping Spread Spectrum and their applications.
Module 6: Equalization, Diversity and Channel coding [6 hrs.]
Fundamentals of equalization, General adaptive equalizer, Linear and non-linear equalizers, diversity techniques, RAKE receivers, Basic concept of coding.
Module 7 Multiple access techniques [5 hrs.]
Introduction, FDMA, TDMA, CDMA, SDMA, the capacity of cellular systems
Module 8: Introduction to Multicarrier systems [5 hrs.]
OFDM and wireless LAN, WiMAX, GSM, WCDMA, 3GPP LTE and other 4G standards.

Course Objective

1 .

Understand various mobile standards from 1G to 5G
2 .

To develop skills in the link budget design of the cellular system.
3 .

To analyze the effects of small-scale fading and large-scale path loss.
4 .

To understand the modulation and multiple access techniques used for cellular systems.

Course Outcome

1 .

1) Understanding the basics of mobile and wireless communication and solving various types of problems.
2) Apply theory for analyzing a practical problem related to the mobile communication system.
3) Application of large-scale and small-scale channel models for the design of mobile communication systems.
4) Analyze and design various wireless communication systems.

Essential Reading

1 .

Andrea Goldsmith, Wireless Communication, Cambridge University Press , 2009

2 .

Andreas Molisch, Wireless communications, Wiley , 2nd Edition

Supplementary Reading

1 .

T.S. Rappaport, Wireless Communications – Principles and Practice, Prentice Hall of India/ Pearson , 2nd Edition

2 .

Stuber, Principles of Mobile Communication,, Springer , 2nd Edition

8999.t: EE4306: Dynamics and Control of Biomolecular Systems
8999.b:
Course Details

Subject {L-T-P / C} : EE4306 : Dynamics and Control of Biomolecular Systems { 3-0-0 / 3}

Subject Nature : Theory

Syllabus

Module 1 :

Module-1: Introduction - Cell as a ‘system’, Central dogma of molecular biology, Systems and Synthetic Biology, different dynamics in cellular and molecular biology, Control problems in cellular and molecular biology (Hours: 2)
Module-2: Deterministic modeling – Chemical Reaction Network (CRN) modeling, Law of mass action, Quasi-steady-state approximation, Hill function and cooperativity, modeling gene regulation, modeling signal transduction, modeling enzymatic reactions (Hours: 7)
Module-3: Stochastic modeling – Chemical Master Equation, Chemical Langevin Equation, Stochastic Simulation Algorithm (Hours: 4)
Module-4: Feedback loops – Autoregulation, Negative feedback in cells, Positive feedback in cells, Delay, Oscillatory behavior, limit cycles, Toggle switch (Hours: 7)
Module-5: Feedforward loops – Feedforward loops in cells, Fold change detection (Hours: 3)
Module-6: Control – Antithetic Integral feedback, Robustness and perfect adaptation, Differentiator, PID control in cell (Hours: 5)
Module 7: Design – Recombinant DNA technology, Plasmid design, Promoter and RBS selection (Hours: 3)
Module 8: Interconnection – Retroactivity, Resource competition (Hours: 4)

Course Objective

1 .

Introduce application of systems and control theory in biology.
2 .

Modeling and control of biomolecular systems.
3 .

Design of biomolecular systems.

Course Outcome

1 .

At the end of the course, students will be able to
CO1: Analyze deterministic models of biochemical reaction networks.
CO2. Apply the knowledge of probabilistic modeling for biomolecular reactions.
CO3. Analyze feedback and feedforward loops and their time responses in biology.
CO4. Demonstrate the method of integral feedback to get perfect adaptation in biomolecular systems.
CO5. Design plasmids to get desired dynamics of reporter protein concentration.
CO6: Learn the challenges of designing scalable and modular biomolecular systems and possible solutions.

Essential Reading

1 .

Richard M. Murray and Domitilla Del Vecchio, Biomolecular Feedback Systems, Princeton University Press , http://www.cds.caltech.edu/~murray/books/AM08/pdf/bfs-pupss_13Jun14.pdf

2 .

Uri Alon, An Introduction to Systems Biology, CRC Press

Supplementary Reading

1 .

Eduardo D. Sontag, Lecture Notes in Mathematical Biology, Rutgers University , https://www.di.univr.it/documenti/OccorrenzaIns/matdid/matdid262230.pdf

2 .

Brian P. Ingalls, Mathematical Modeling in Systems Biology, The MIT Press , https://www.math.uwaterloo.ca/~bingalls/MMSB/Notes.pdf

Journal and Conferences

1 .

Hsiao, V., Swaminathan, A., & Murray, R. M. (2018). Control theory for synthetic biology: recent advances in system characterization, control design, and controller implementation for synthetic biology. IEEE Control Systems Magazine, 38(3), 32-62.
2 .

Del Vecchio, D., Qian, Y., Murray, R. M., & Sontag, E. D. (2018). Future systems and control research in synthetic biology. Annual Reviews in Control, 45, 5-17.

Subject Nature : Theory

Processes and techniques
